title: Positive profinite Cech exactness for norm-topological algebraic scalars
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] with its extended nonarchimedean norm topology, and use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A profinite set means a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space. For a continuous surjection $q:T\to V$ of profinite sets and $n\geq0$, put
$$T_V^{n+1}=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_n)\in T^{n+1}:q(t_0)=\cdots=q(t_n)\},\qquad C^n(q)=C(T_V^{n+1},\Omega),$$
with the subspace topology and all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Give these additive groups the differential
$$(d^nf)(t_0,\ldots,t_{n+1})=\sum_{j=0}^{n+1}(-1)^jf(t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_{n+1}).$$
The following is the corrected noncomplete-coefficient statement.

(1) Global positive exactness fails in general: there exist nonempty metrizable profinite $T,V$, a continuous surjection $q:T\to V$, and $f\in C^1(q)$ with $d^1f=0$, such that there is no $g\in C^0(q)$ with $d^0g=f$.

(2) The split-cover and local replacement holds in every positive degree. If $q$ has a continuous section $\sigma:V\to T$, then for every $n\geq1$ and $f\in C^n(q)$ with $d^nf=0$, the formula
$$g(t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})=f(\sigma(q(t_0)),t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})$$
defines a continuous $g$ with $d^{n-1}g=f$. For an arbitrary $q$, let $q':T\times_VT\to T$ be the first projection. The pullback of $f$ to the nerve of $q'$ has the continuous primitive
$$h(s;t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})=f(s,t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1}),$$
where all displayed points have the same $q$-image. Thus this positive exactness is valid after the profinite base change $T\to V$. The empty surjection is included in (2). All equalities concern the actual $\Omega$-valued functions, without completion, closure of images, or finite-subextension-valued replacement.

proof.text: For clause (1), choose $q:T\to V$ and $(t_k^-,t_k^+)$ from [lem-sfb-countable-split-profinite-cover]. Thus every nonempty open subset of $T$ contains both points of some double fibre with arbitrarily large index, and the two oriented off-diagonal points of each such fibre are clopen in $R=T\times_VT$. These are the exact topological properties used below; no continuous section of $q$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algcl-countable-closed-finite-cover] with the finite intermediate field $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. It gives increasing closed intermediate fields $F_k\subseteq\Omega$, finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with $\Omega=\bigcup_kF_k$. In particular $F_j\subseteq F_k$ whenever $j\leq k$, and for any continuous $g:T\to\Omega$ the subsets $g^{-1}(F_j)$ are closed and cover $T$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3: countability of finite subextensions. The cited node supplies the increasing closed cover, not a finite-stage factorization of a continuous function.

proof.text: For each $k$, apply [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] to the finite extension $F_k$ with the restricted norm and choose a uniformizer $\pi_k$. Its conclusions give $0<|\pi_k|<1$, units of norm $1$, and $x=u\pi_k^m$ for $x\in F_k^\times$, $m\in\mathbf Z$. By algebraic closedness [def-weil-algebraic-closure] choose $b_k\in\Omega$ with $b_k^2=\pi_k$. It is outside $F_k$: otherwise $|b_k|=|\pi_k|^m$ for an integer $m$, so $|\pi_k|^{2m}=|\pi_k|$, forcing $2m=1$. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $|\ell|=\ell^{-1}<1$. Choose an integer $M_k\geq0$ with $|\ell|^{M_k}|b_k|\leq\ell^{-k}$, and put $a_k=\ell^{M_k}b_k$. Then $|a_k|\leq\ell^{-k}$, hence $a_k\to0$, while $a_k\notin F_k$ because the nonzero scalar $\ell^{M_k}$ and its inverse belong to $F_k$.

proof.text:
Define $f:R\to\Omega$ by $f(x,x)=0$, $f(t_k^-,t_k^+)=a_k$ and $f(t_k^+,t_k^-)=-a_k$. The fibre classification in [lem-sfb-countable-split-profinite-cover] exhausts $R$, so this defines an actual function. For each $N$, the function $f_N$ with these values for $k<N$ and zero elsewhere is continuous: its finitely many nonzero loci are clopen singletons. Given $\epsilon>0$, choose $N$ with $\ell^{-N}<\epsilon$. Around any $z\in R$ choose an open neighbourhood where $f_N$ is constant. On that neighbourhood the ultrametric inequality gives
$$|f(y)-f(z)|\leq\max(|f(y)-f_N(y)|,|f(z)-f_N(z)|)\leq\ell^{-N}<\epsilon.$$
This proves continuity into $\Omega$ itself; no infinite sum is used to define $f$.

proof.text:
Every tuple in $T_V^3$ lies in a fibre of cardinality one or two. On a singleton fibre put $u=0$. On the fibre $\{t_k^-,t_k^+\}$ put $u(t_k^-)=0$ and $u(t_k^+)=a_k$. On each individual fibre $f(x,y)=u(y)-u(x)$, so
$$f(y,z)-f(x,z)+f(x,y)=(u(z)-u(y))-(u(z)-u(x))+(u(y)-u(x))=0.$$
Hence $d^1f=0$. These fibrewise functions $u$ are used only for this algebraic identity; no global continuity of them is claimed.

proof.text:
Suppose a continuous $g:T\to\Omega$ satisfied $g(y)-g(x)=f(x,y)$. The closed sets $A_j=g^{-1}(F_j)$ cover the nonempty compact Hausdorff space $T$ by [lem-sfb-algcl-countable-closed-finite-cover]. Apply [lem-sfb-baire-closed-cover-interior] to $Y=X=T$ and $I=\mathbf N$: a compact Hausdorff space is locally compact, since the whole space is a compact neighbourhood of every point. Thus some $A_j$ contains a nonempty open subset $U$ of $T$. By [lem-sfb-countable-split-profinite-cover], choose $k\geq j$ with $t_k^-,t_k^+\in U$. Then
$$a_k=f(t_k^-,t_k^+)=g(t_k^+)-g(t_k^-)\in F_j\subseteq F_k,$$
contradicting step 3. This proves clause (1), with equality of cochains rather than any statement about closures.

source.place: Tag 0CQN (lemma-baire-category-locally-compact), closed-cover consequence; agent application to the arithmetic cover and the split Cantor relation.

proof.text:
For clause (2), suppose $q\sigma=\mathrm{id}_V$. The map
$$(t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})\longmapsto(\sigma(q(t_0)),t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})$$
is continuous into $T_V^{n+1}$: its coordinates are continuous and the equal-image equations follow from $q\sigma=\mathrm{id}_V$. Thus the displayed $g$ is continuous. Apply $d^nf=0$ to $(\sigma(v),t_0,\ldots,t_n)$, where $v=q(t_i)$ for every $i$. Its first summand is $f(t_0,\ldots,t_n)$; the remaining summands give
$$0=f(t_0,\ldots,t_n)-\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jf(\sigma(v),t_0,\ldots,\widehat{t_j},\ldots,t_n)=f-d^{n-1}g.$$
The equality uses $\sigma(q(t_i))=\sigma(v)$ for every face, including deletion of $t_0$. It works for $n=1$.

proof.text:
For any $q$, [lem-sfb-finite-quotient-fiber-product] applied to $T\to V\leftarrow T$ makes $T\times_VT$ profinite. The projection $q':T\times_VT\to T$ is continuous and has the continuous diagonal section $s\mapsto(s,s)$, so is surjective. Its $(n+1)$-fold fibre product over $T$ consists of $(s;t_0,\ldots,t_n)$ with all $q$-images equal; the tuple maps in both directions are coordinate maps and are continuous for the subspace topologies. Pullback sends $f$ to $(s;t_0,\ldots,t_n)\mapsto f(t_0,\ldots,t_n)$ and commutes with each coordinate deletion, hence preserves the cocycle equation. Step 7 with the diagonal section gives exactly
$$h(s;t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})=f(s,t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})$$
and $d^{n-1}h=q^*f$. If $T=V=\varnothing$, all these function groups are zero, and the same formulas are the unique zero functions. This completes clause (2).

The old global claim is false: every positive-degree Cech cocycle in C(T_V^{n+1},Omega) for noncomplete Omega = algebraic closure of Q_l was said to have a continuous primitive. I checked the counterexample independently. The cover is the graph closure over Cantor space with eventually-alternating sequences split in two. Over v not in D the fibres are singletons, because the lexicographic comparisons are locally constant. Over v_k there are exactly two points, since v_k is approached from both sides by eventually constant sequences. The oriented pairs are clopen in R by a kth-bit condition, and tail density holds via B = V minus q(T minus U). The cocycle f with values a_k, |a_k| <= l^-k, is a uniform limit of continuous f_N, and d^1 f = 0 holds through a fibrewise potential. No continuous primitive g exists: Baire on g^-1(F_j) gives a_k in F_j, contained in F_k. a_k is not in F_k: if b_k^2 = pi_k with b_k in F_k, then 2m = 1. Clause (2) contraction signs checked, including the t_0 face, n=1, the base change via the diagonal section of q', and the empty case. The correction is legitimate under brief-stage1 section 1 and E7, is named in the report, and no target or unit statement is touched.
